newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end lower on budget uncertainties.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end lower on budget uncertainties.

text.p: Delhi shares ended lower on Monday on nervous selling by operators and foreign investors, prompted by uncertainty over the passage of the federal budget for 1997/98 (April-March), brokers said.
The Delhi bourse's benchmark index fell 2.01 points to close at 745.68.
"Purchases by domestic financial institutions were insufficient to arrest the falling prices on the Delhi bourse," said Vinod Gupta of brokers Fairdeal Investments.
India's ruling United Front alliance said on Monday its steering committee will hold talks on the budget on April 9 to seek its passage through parliament.
The ruling coalition will approach other political parties through the speaker and try to evolve a consensus view.

"We will take a collective view on the budget and after that we will get in touch with the speaker (of the lower house of parliament) and other parties and evolve consensus view," United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy told reporters.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda faces a vote of confidence on April 11 following the decision by the Congress party, his former make-or-break ally, to withdraw support to the 10-month-old government.
State Bank of India quoted 6.75 rupees lower at 266.25.
